defects: Pairwise inequivalence hypothesis (¬IsEquiv) is replaced by mere pairwise inequality (v i ≠ v j), which is strictly weaker — two distinct but equivalent absolute values (e.g. one a power of the other) would satisfy the produced hypothesis but violate the actual theorem's requirement, making the produced statement a different and generally false proposition

The conclusion's codomain is plain (ι → F) with no topology tied to the absolute values v i (no use of WithAbs or any per-factor topology), so it fails to state that each factor carries the topology induced by v i; without an ambient TopologicalSpace F instance the DenseRange statement is either vacuous/ill-formed or refers to an unrelated topology, losing the entire point of the density claim
Fintype ι used instead of Finite ι — a stronger (data-carrying) typeclass assumption than the Prop-valued Finite used in gold, a structural mismatch beyond mere reformulation
hv_nontrivial correctly unfolds IsNontrivial but is stated with explicit existential rather than the named predicate — acceptable spelling difference on its own, though moot given the other defects
